output.summary: An annual mustard native to the deserts of North Africa and the Middle East, Saharan mustard has spreading stems and relatively subdued yellow flowers. When wet, its seed coats form a sticky gel that helps seeds cling to people, animals and objects. It is also used in North African cuisine, including the Libyan dish Couscous bil Aslooz.
output.edibilityNote: Used in North African cuisine, including the traditional Libyan dish Couscous bil Aslooz.
